# Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI

**Project:** Retain & Recommend AI — Returns-Aware Product Recommendation, Customer Lapse Prediction & RAG-Powered Retention Agent
**Document type:** Knowledge Base file 1 of 3 (business guidance for the retention agent)
**Companion files:** `promotion_policy.md` (discount and promotion rules), `business_rules_kpis.md` (definitions, formulas, thresholds, data rules)
**Version:** 1.1 — risk tiers aligned with the supplied scoring file `customer_lapse_predictions.csv` (three tiers: Low, Medium, High).
**Status:** All thresholds other than the source-file tiers are proposals until validated and approved by the business.

---

## 0. How to Use This Document

### 0.1 Purpose
This playbook tells the AI Agent how to reason about customer retention for a wholesale business: which customers to look at first, what kind of action to consider, when to involve a human, and how to describe results honestly.

### 0.2 Evidence Labels
Every passage in the Knowledge Base uses these labels. The AI Agent must preserve them when quoting or paraphrasing.

| Label | Meaning | Agent behavior |

|---|---|---|

| `Verified Fact` | Established definition or statement confirmed by the business or by its data. | May state as fact. |

| `Proposed Assumption` | Reasonable working value or framework chosen by the author, not confirmed. | State as an assumption; never as a confirmed fact. |

| `Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval` | A rule suggested for the business to adopt. | Never treat as approved policy. Say it is proposed. |

| `Pending Validation` | Value or claim that must be tested on real data before operational use. | Disclose that it is unvalidated. |

### 0.3 Core Principle: Knowledge Base vs. Structured Data

- **`Verified Fact`** — The Knowledge Base supplies *business guidance, definitions, and policy*. It never supplies customer-specific values.

- **`Verified Fact`** — Customer-specific values (lapse probability, risk tier, value tier, recommended products, cancellation probability, purchase history) must come from actual model outputs or structured data supplied at run time.

- **Guardrail G-1:** If a customer-specific value is not present in the supplied model output or structured data, the AI Agent must state "value not available" and must not estimate, infer, or fabricate it.

## 1. Customer Lapse and Churn Concepts

### 1.1 Definitions

- **Lapse** — A customer who was active has stopped purchasing for a defined period. In this project, lapse is defined operationally on a time basis (see 1.2).

- **Churn** — A permanent or long-term end of the customer relationship. **`Verified Fact`** — Churn cannot be observed directly in non-contractual wholesale data, because a customer can simply return later. The project therefore predicts **lapse**, not churn.

- **Non-contractual setting** — **`Proposed Assumption`** — The wholesale customers are not bound by subscriptions, so no formal cancellation event marks the end of the relationship. Confirm with the business.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 1. Customer Lapse and Churn Concepts > 1.1 Definitions

text:
so no formal cancellation event marks the end of the relationship. Confirm with the business.
- **Active customer** — A customer with at least one valid purchase in the observation window ending at the prediction timestamp.

- **Lapsed customer (observed)** — **`Proposed Assumption`** — A customer with zero valid purchases in the 90 days after a prediction timestamp (the label used to train the model) or, for current operations, zero valid purchases in the most recent 90 days.

- **Predicted lapse risk** — The model's estimated probability (p_lapse, between 0 and 1) that an active customer will make zero valid purchases in the next 90 days.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 1. Customer Lapse and Churn Concepts > 1.1 Definitions

text:
### 1.2 Lapse vs. Churn vs. Cancellation (do not confuse)
| Term | What it describes | Where it is measured |
|---|---|---|
| Lapse | Absence of valid purchases over the horizon | Customer level |
| Churn | Permanent departure | Not directly observable |
| Cancellation | A cancelled order or invoice | Transaction level |
| Return | Goods sent back after delivery | Transaction level, if recorded separately |

- **`Data Gap`** — Whether the source data distinguishes returns from order cancellations is unconfirmed. Until confirmed, the Agent must use the term "cancellation" only for records the data flags as cancellations and must not describe them as customer dissatisfaction.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 1. Customer Lapse and Churn Concepts > 1.2 Lapse vs. Churn vs. Cancellation (do not confuse)

text:
### 1.3 Why Lapse Matters in Wholesale
- **`Proposed Assumption`** — Wholesale revenue is concentrated in a minority of customers, so losing a few high-value accounts may affect revenue disproportionately. This must be verified with the business's actual revenue concentration (see `business_rules_kpis.md`, Section 12).
- Wholesale purchasing is often irregular or seasonal. A long gap is not always a warning sign; it may be a normal buying cycle. The Agent must compare a customer's current gap against that customer's own typical purchase interval, when available.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 1. Customer Lapse and Churn Concepts > 1.3 Why Lapse Matters in Wholesale

text:
### 1.4 Warning Signals (Behavioral Indicators)
Signals the Agent may reference **only if present in the structured data**:
- Increasing days since last purchase (recency) relative to the customer's usual inter-purchase interval.
- Falling purchase frequency versus the previous period.
- Falling order value or net revenue versus the previous period.
- Narrowing product variety.
- Rising cancellation count or cancellation rate.
- Shift from regular to sporadic purchasing.

**Guardrail G-3:** These signals are associations used by the model, not proven causes of lapse. The Agent must not claim that a signal *causes* lapse.

## 2. Customer Risk Segmentation

### 2.1 Risk Tiers
**`Verified Fact`** — The scoring file assigns each customer to one of three categories in the column `risk_category`. The observed ranges of `lapse_probability` in the file are: Low up to 0.2977, Medium 0.3001 to 0.4987, High 0.5005 and above. The implied cut points are 0.30 and 0.50. The exact boundary convention (inclusive or exclusive) is a `Data Gap` to confirm with the model owner.

| Risk tier | p_lapse range | Customers in the supplied file (snapshot 2011-09-01) | Plain-language meaning | Typical stance |

| Low | < 0.30 | 657 (12.6%) | Model sees continued purchasing as likely. | Maintain; no intervention needed. |
| Medium | 0.30 to < 0.50 | 548 (10.5%) | Meaningful uncertainty; early signs may be present. | Monitor and light-touch engagement. |
| High | ≥ 0.50 | 4,019 (77.0%) | Lapse is more likely than not, according to the model. | Active, personalized outreach, prioritized by the Focus List. |

### 2.2 Interpretation Rules
- A risk tier is a **model-based estimate**, not a fact about the customer's intention.
- A p_lapse of 0.70 means the model assigns a 70% estimated chance under its assumptions, if calibrated. It does **not** mean the customer will lapse, and it is **not** a monetary amount.
- **Guardrail G-4:** The Agent must always report the tier together with its source (model name or version, prediction timestamp). **`Data Gap`** — model name and version are not specified in this Knowledge Base.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 2. Customer Risk Segmentation > 2.2 Interpretation Rules

text:
### 2.3 Special Flags (Overlay on Risk Tier)
Flags are evaluated from structured data. Definitions and thresholds are in `business_rules_kpis.md`, Section 9.4.

| Flag | Short definition | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Repeated Cancellation Flag (RCF) | ≥ 3 cancellations in W_obs, or value-based cancellation rate ≥ 0.20 with ≥ 3 invoices | `Proposed Assumption`, `Pending Validation` |
| Declining Activity Flag (DAF) | Purchase count or net revenue in last 90 days < 50% of the previous 90 days, with ≥ 2 purchases in the previous 90 days | `Proposed Assumption`, `Pending Validation` |
| Limited History Flag (LHF) | Only 1 valid purchase in W_obs | `Proposed Assumption` |
| Already Lapsed | No valid purchase in the most recent 90 days | `Proposed Assumption` |

## 3. Recommended Actions by Customer Segment

All actions below are **recommendations for human decision-makers**. They are `Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval`. Any action involving a discount follows `promotion_policy.md`.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Recommended Actions by Customer Segment

text:
### 3.1 Low Risk
- **Goal:** Preserve the relationship efficiently.
- **Recommended actions:** Standard communication; routine account contact; relevant product suggestions based on purchase history.
- **Avoid:** Discounts, special offers, or heavy outreach. See `promotion_policy.md`, Section 6 (avoiding unnecessary discounts).
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Recommended Actions by Customer Segment > 3.1 Low Risk

text:
### 3.2 Medium Risk
- **Goal:** Detect and address early drift.
- **Recommended actions:** Check-in message or call; product recommendations tied to previously purchased categories; confirm that service or availability issues are not present.
- **Escalate if:** Medium risk is combined with RCF, DAF, or V1 value tier. See Section 8.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Recommended Actions by Customer Segment > 3.2 Medium Risk

text:
### 3.3 High Risk
- **Goal:** Re-engage before lapse occurs.
- **Recommended actions:** Personal outreach by an account owner; tailored product recommendations (Section 6); service-recovery conversation if cancellations are present; consider a non-discount incentive first (for example, priority availability, flexible ordering support) before any price-based offer.
- **Promotion:** Eligible for **review** only. See `promotion_policy.md`, Section 8.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Recommended Actions by Customer Segment > 3.3 High Risk

text:
### 3.4 High Risk — Focus List (Highest Urgency)
- **Definition:** High-risk customers who rank in the top N by Priority Score (Section 5.5), including all P1 customers. N is set by the business (`Data Gap`).
- **Goal:** Intervene early, with human ownership, where urgency and business importance are greatest.
- **Recommended actions:** **`Human Review Required`** for the action plan; direct contact by a senior account owner; root-cause conversation; tailored recommendation list; any incentive must go through approval.
- **Guardrail G-5:** The Agent may draft a retention strategy but must not send communications or commit to terms.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Recommended Actions by Customer Segment > 3.4 High Risk — Focus List (Highest Urgency)

text:
### 3.5 Already Lapsed (Reactivation)
- **Goal:** Win back a customer with no valid purchase in the last 90 days.
- **Recommended actions:** Reactivation message referencing previously purchased categories; confirm the relationship status with the account owner; avoid assuming the customer is lost permanently.
- **`Data Gap`** — The point at which a lapsed customer is treated as permanently lost (for example, 12 months) is not specified. **`Proposed Assumption`** — Use a business-defined cutoff; confirm before use.
- **Evaluation caution:** Reactivation outcomes must be compared with a control group to avoid crediting normal returning behavior to the campaign (Section 11).
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Recommended Actions by Customer Segment > 3.5 Already Lapsed (Reactivation)

text:
### 3.6 New and Limited-History Customers
- **Goal:** Build a purchasing habit.
- **Guidance:** With few observations, model estimates are less reliable. The Agent must flag low confidence when the Limited History Flag is present, and must not over-interpret p_lapse.

---
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Recommended Actions by Customer Segment > 3.6 New and Limited-History Customers

## 4. Handling Repeated Cancellations and Declining Activity

### 4.1 Repeated Cancellations
**`Verified Fact`** — Cancellations may reflect many causes: stock-outs, pricing errors, ordering mistakes, delivery problems, customer cash-flow issues, or internal data practices.

**Guardrail G-6:** The Agent must not assume that cancellations indicate dissatisfaction, and must not blame the customer.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 4. Handling Repeated Cancellations and Declining Activity > 4.1 Repeated Cancellations

text:
Agent must not assume that cancellations indicate dissatisfaction, and must not blame the customer.
Recommended handling when the RCF is present:
1. **Diagnose before acting.** **`Human Review Required`** — An account owner should review the cancelled orders and their reasons. **`Data Gap`** — cancellation reason codes are not confirmed.
2. **Check operational causes.** Availability, lead time, pricing errors, and picking or delivery problems.
3. **Prefer service recovery over discounts.** A discount does not fix an availability or ordering-process problem.
4. **Adjust recommendations.** Down-rank products with a high estimated cancellation risk for that customer (Section 6.3).
5. **Do not reward cancellation behavior.** Do not offer a promotion whose main effect would be to encourage repeated order-and-cancel cycles (see `promotion_policy.md`, Section 5).
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 4. Handling Repeated Cancellations and Declining Activity > 4.1 Repeated Cancellations

text:
### 4.2 Declining Purchase Activity
When the DAF is present:
1. Compare the customer's recent gap with their own historical rhythm; seasonality may explain the decline.
2. Look at which categories declined. A fall in one category may indicate a competitor win or a stock issue.
3. Recommend outreach that asks about needs, not only offers.
4. Escalate when the DAF is combined with a V1 or V2 value tier and High risk.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 4. Handling Repeated Cancellations and Declining Activity > 4.2 Declining Purchase Activity

text:
### 4.3 Both Flags Together (RCF + DAF)
- **`Human Review Required`** — mandatory. Treat as a priority account review, because instability and falling activity together indicate a possible service or relationship problem.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 4. Handling Repeated Cancellations and Declining Activity > 4.3 Both Flags Together (RCF + DAF)

text:
### 4.4 Interaction Summary
| Situation | Suggested primary lever | Promotion stance |
|---|---|---|
| High risk, no flags | Personal outreach + relevant products | Eligible for review |
| High risk + RCF | Service recovery, root-cause review | Requires approval; discount not the first lever |
| High risk + DAF | Needs conversation, category review | Eligible for review |
| Focus List + RCF + DAF | Senior account review | Requires approval |
| Low risk + RCF | Operational review only | Not recommended |

## 5. Customer Prioritization

### 5.1 Principle
Prioritization must combine **how likely** a customer is to lapse with **how much the customer matters to the business**. Reviewing only high-risk customers wastes effort on low-value accounts; reviewing only high-value customers ignores urgency.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 5. Customer Prioritization > 5.1 Principle

text:
### 5.2 Value Tiers
**`Proposed Assumption`**, **`Pending Validation`** — based on historical net revenue in W_obs (percentile among active customers).

| Value tier | Rule |
|---|---|
| V1 (High value) | ≥ 90th percentile |
| V2 (Mid value) | 60th to < 90th percentile |
| V3 (Lower value) | < 60th percentile |

**Limitation:** Historical net revenue is neither profit nor future value (see `business_rules_kpis.md`, Section 14). **`Data Gap`** — customer-level margin data is not confirmed.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 5. Customer Prioritization > 5.2 Value Tiers

text:
### 5.3 Priority Matrix
**`Proposed Assumption`**, **`Pending Validation`**

| Risk tier \ Value tier | V1 | V2 | V3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | P1 | P2 | P3 |
| Medium | P2 | P3 | P4 |
| Low | P3 | P4 | P4 |

| Priority | Interpretation | Expected handling |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | High urgency, high importance | Immediate human-owned review |
| P2 | Important or urgent | Review within the next planning cycle |
| P3 | Moderate | Light-touch or batched outreach |
| P4 | Low | Monitor; automated standard communication only |
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 5. Customer Prioritization > 5.3 Priority Matrix

text:
### 5.4 Ordering Within a Band
Within a priority band, the Agent may order customers by the dimensionless Priority Score:

```
Priority Score = p_lapse × V_norm
```
- `p_lapse` — model probability, 0 to 1.
- `V_norm` — percentile rank of the customer's historical net revenue in W_obs, scaled to (0, 1].
- **Unit:** none. **Guardrail G-7:** Priority Score is a ranking aid. It is not a monetary amount, a probability, or an expected loss.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 5. Customer Prioritization > 5.4 Ordering Within a Band

text:
### 5.5 Focus List (Replaces the Former Critical Tier)
**`Proposed Assumption`** — Because the High tier holds most customers in the supplied file, band assignment alone does not limit workload. The Focus List is the practical review queue:
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 5. Customer Prioritization > 5.5 Focus List (Replaces the Former Critical Tier)

text:
file, band assignment alone does not limit workload. The Focus List is the practical review queue:
```
Focus List = the N High-risk customers with the highest Priority Score
```
- **N** is the business's review capacity per cycle. **`Data Gap`** — N is not specified. The Agent must not assume a value.
- **Input dependency:** Priority Score needs a value measure (`V_norm`), which is not in the scoring file. Until value data is joined by `customer_id`, the Agent may only order High-risk customers by `p_lapse` and must state that business value was not considered.
- **Ties:** Break ties by higher `V_norm`, then by higher p_lapse, then by `customer_id` for reproducibility.

## 6. Product Recommendation Considerations

### 6.1 Purpose in Retention
Relevant recommendations reduce the effort for a customer to place the next order. They are a **retention support tool**, not a guarantee of purchase.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 6. Product Recommendation Considerations > 6.1 Purpose in Retention

text:
### 6.2 Inputs the Agent May Use
Only from supplied structured data or model output:
- Predicted purchase likelihood (p_buy) per customer and product.
- Predicted cancellation risk (p_cancel) per customer and product, or per product if customer-level is unavailable.
- Product availability and stock status.
- Product business value indicator (revenue or margin proxy, if available).
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 6. Product Recommendation Considerations > 6.2 Inputs the Agent May Use

text:
### 6.3 Returns-Aware (Cancellation-Aware) Ranking
The project uses cancellation risk to avoid recommending items likely to be ordered and then cancelled. The ranking logic is defined in `business_rules_kpis.md`, Section 10:

```
Adjusted Recommendation Score = p_buy × (1 − p_cancel) × Value_norm × Availability_flag
```
- All components are unitless; the result is a ranking score, not a monetary amount.
- **`Pending Validation`** — The multiplicative form is a proposed design.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 6. Product Recommendation Considerations > 6.3 Returns-Aware (Cancellation-Aware) Ranking

text:
### 6.4 Recommendation Guardrails
- **Guardrail G-8:** Do not recommend products flagged unavailable, discontinued, or restricted.
- **Guardrail G-9:** Do not recommend a product on the basis of a discount unless the promotion was approved under `promotion_policy.md`.
- **Guardrail G-10:** Explain recommendations using only the signals actually supplied (for example, "previously purchased in this category"). Do not invent reasons.
- **Guardrail G-11:** A recommendation list is a suggestion for a human-reviewed conversation. It is not a commitment of stock or price.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 6. Product Recommendation Considerations > 6.4 Recommendation Guardrails

text:
### 6.5 Diversity and Fatigue
**`Proposed Assumption`** — Offering a few relevant products is generally preferable to a long list. The Agent should keep lists short and relevant. The ideal list length is `Data Gap`.

---
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 6. Product Recommendation Considerations > 6.5 Diversity and Fatigue

text:
## 7. Personalized Retention Strategies

### 7.1 Strategy Building Blocks
| Block | Use when | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Relationship contact | Any High risk | Account owner assignment (`Data Gap` if absent) |
| Product recommendations | Narrowing variety or declining activity | Recommendation model output |
| Service recovery | RCF present | Cancellation detail |
| Replenishment reminder | Customer has a regular reorder cycle | Purchase interval data |
| Availability priority | Customer affected by stock issues | Stock data |
| Promotion (review) | Only after non-price levers considered | Approval per `promotion_policy.md` |
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 7. Personalized Retention Strategies > 7.1 Strategy Building Blocks

text:
### 7.2 Personalization Rules
- Base every strategy on supplied customer data. Cite which fields drove it.
- Match tone and offering to the customer's value tier and purchasing history.
- Prefer the **least costly effective action** first: contact before incentive, incentive before discount.
- State uncertainty: any strategy is a hypothesis about what may help.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 7. Personalized Retention Strategies > 7.2 Personalization Rules

text:
### 7.3 Required Content of an Agent-Generated Retention Strategy
Each strategy output must contain:
1. Customer identifier (as supplied).
2. Risk tier, p_lapse, prediction timestamp, source (model/version if available).
3. Value tier and priority band.
4. Active flags (RCF, DAF, LHF).
5. Key signals used (from data only).
6. Recommended action(s) and rationale, citing the playbook section.
7. Product suggestions (if available) with scores labeled as scores.
8. Promotion stance per `promotion_policy.md` (Not Recommended, Eligible for Review, or Requires Approval).
9. Human-review status.
10. Limitations and missing data.

---
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 7. Personalized Retention Strategies > 7.3 Required Content of an Agent-Generated Retention Strategy

## 8. Recommended Agent Decision Workflow

### 8.1 Step-by-Step Workflow

1. **Receive input.** Confirm that structured data and model outputs for the customer are present. If not, state which values are missing and stop (Guardrail G-1).

2. **Validate data quality.** Check for missing prediction timestamp, missing p_lapse, or out-of-range values. If invalid, flag a **Data Gap** and escalate.

3. **Identify the segment.** Assign the risk tier, value tier, and flags using the rules in this Knowledge Base.

4. **Determine priority.** Look up the band in Section 5.3.

5. **Retrieve guidance.** Retrieve the relevant segment actions (Section 3) and flag handling (Section 4).

6. **Assess recommendations.** Use model-provided product scores and apply the availability and cancellation guardrails.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 8. Recommended Agent Decision Workflow > 8.1 Step-by-Step Workflow

text:
Use model-provided product scores and apply the availability and cancellation guardrails.
7. **Assess promotion stance.** Apply `promotion_policy.md` decision matrix. Default to **Not Recommended** when information is incomplete.

8. **Check human-review triggers.** Apply Section 9.

9. **Generate the output** with the content required in 7.3.

10. **Log for audit** (see `promotion_policy.md`, Section 9, and `business_rules_kpis.md`, Section 16).

### 8.3 Default Behaviors When Information Is Missing
| Missing item | Agent behavior |
|---|---|
| p_lapse | Do not assign a risk tier. Report Data Gap. |
| Value tier inputs | Assign "value unknown"; do not default to V3. Escalate for priority decisions. |
| Cancellation data | Skip RCF assessment and say it was not evaluated. |
| Margin data | Do not claim profitability. |
| Stock data | Do not recommend as available; mark "availability unconfirmed". |

## 10. Retention KPI Interpretation and Limitations

KPI definitions and formulas are in `business_rules_kpis.md`, Sections 11 to 13. This section covers interpretation.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 10. Retention KPI Interpretation and Limitations

text:
### 10.1 How to Read Retention KPIs
| KPI | Reading guidance | Common misreading |
|---|---|---|
| Retention rate | Share of a baseline cohort active in a later period. | Treating it as the effect of the program. |
| Lapse rate | Share of a cohort with no purchase over the horizon. | Treating lapse as permanent loss. |
| Reactivation rate | Share of lapsed customers who purchased again. | Crediting all reactivations to a campaign. |
| Cancellation rate | Share of orders (or value) cancelled. | Assuming cancellations indicate poor customer attitude. |
| Net revenue of retained customers | Revenue from customers who stayed. | Treating it as profit. |
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 10. Retention KPI Interpretation and Limitations > 10.1 How to Read Retention KPIs

text:
### 10.2 Evaluation Limitations

- **Correlation is not causation.** **`Verified Fact`** — Observed changes after an action do not prove the action caused them.

- **Selection bias.** Customers chosen for outreach are chosen because they are high-risk; comparing them with low-risk customers is misleading.

- **Regression to the mean.** Customers with extreme short-term drops may recover without intervention.

- **Seasonality.** Wholesale cycles can mimic lapse or recovery.

- **Small numbers.** Rates from small groups are unstable; state group sizes.

- **Censoring.** Recent cohorts have not completed the full horizon, so their outcomes are incomplete.
section: Retention Playbook — Retain & Recommend AI > 10. Retention KPI Interpretation and Limitations > 10.2 Evaluation Limitations

- Say "associated with" or "the model indicates", not "caused by".
- Say "estimated" for any model output.

### Example 1 — High Risk, High Value, On the Focus List

# Promotion Policy — Retain & Recommend AI

**Project:** Retain & Recommend AI — Returns-Aware Product Recommendation, Customer Lapse Prediction & RAG-Powered Retention Agent
**Document type:** Knowledge Base file 2 of 3 (promotion and discount decision policy)
**Companion files:** `retention_playbook.md` (retention actions), `business_rules_kpis.md` (definitions, formulas, thresholds)
**Version:** 1.1 — risk tiers aligned with the supplied scoring file `customer_lapse_predictions.csv` (Low, Medium, High)

## 0. Critical Notice and Reading Rules

### 0.1 No Approved Company Policy Is Included
**`Verified Fact`** — This document does **not** contain a company's approved discount limits, margin requirements, budgets, or eligibility rules. None were provided to the author.

**`Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval`** — Every rule below that sets a limit, condition, or decision outcome is a proposal. The AI Agent must **never treat a proposed rule as approved business policy**, must not present proposed rules to customers or staff as binding, and must disclose their proposed status when citing them.

Where a number would normally appear, this document uses a named placeholder. Placeholders have no value until the business sets them. The Agent must not guess a value.

| Placeholder | Meaning | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `D_MAX_[tier]` | Maximum discount percentage permitted for a category of promotion | `Data Gap` — not set |
| `M_MIN` | Minimum acceptable margin after discount | `Data Gap` — not set |
| `B_PERIOD` | Promotion budget for a defined period | `Data Gap` — not set |
| `B_CUSTOMER` | Maximum promotion spend per customer per period | `Data Gap` — not set |
| `N_COOLDOWN` | Minimum days between promotions to the same customer | `Data Gap` — not set |
| `APPROVER_ROLE_[n]` | Role entitled to approve at a given level | `Data Gap` — not set |

### 0.3 Evidence Labels
`Verified Fact`, `Proposed Assumption`, `Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval`, `Pending Validation`, `Data Gap`, `Human Review Required`. Definitions are in `retention_playbook.md`, Section 0.2.
section: Promotion Policy — Retain & Recommend AI > 0. Critical Notice and Reading Rules > 0.3 Evidence Labels

### 0.4 Customer-Specific Inputs
- **Guardrail PG-1:** Customer risk tier, value tier, flags, and product scores used in promotion decisions must come from actual model outputs or structured data. If missing, the decision outcome is **Not Recommended** until the data is supplied.
- **Guardrail PG-2:** The Agent must never state or imply that a model score or priority score is a monetary amount, a profit figure, or a guaranteed return from a promotion.

### 0.5 Shared Terms (Consistent With Other Files)
- **Risk tiers:** Low (p_lapse < 0.30), Medium (0.30 to < 0.50), High (≥ 0.50). `Verified Fact` for the ranges observed in `customer_lapse_predictions.csv`; business meaning `Pending Validation`. The earlier Critical tier has been retired.
- **Focus List:** The top N High-risk customers by Priority Score (`retention_playbook.md`, Section 5.5). N is a `Data Gap`.
- **Value tiers:** V1 (≥ 90th percentile of historical net revenue), V2 (60th to < 90th), V3 (< 60th). `Proposed Assumption`, `Pending Validation`.
- **Flags:** Repeated Cancellation Flag (RCF), Declining Activity Flag (DAF), Limited History Flag (LHF).
- **Priority bands:** P1 to P4 (see `retention_playbook.md`, Section 5.3).

## 1. Purpose and Principles

### 1.1 Purpose
The promotion policy ensures that incentives are used deliberately for retention, protect profitability, and remain auditable.
section: Promotion Policy — Retain & Recommend AI > 1. Purpose and Principles > 1.1 Purpose

text:
### 1.2 Principles
`Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval`
1. **Last resort, not first lever.** Use non-price retention actions first (service recovery, outreach, availability support).
2. **Need-based.** A promotion should respond to a documented retention need (risk, decline, or a specific barrier), not to routine behavior.
3. **Smallest effective incentive.** Use the lowest-cost incentive that plausibly addresses the need.
4. **Profit-protective.** Do not recommend a promotion whose profitability cannot be assessed.
5. **Human-approved.** The Agent recommends; people decide.
6. **Auditable.** Every recommendation is logged with its inputs and rule references.
7. **Fair and consistent.** Similar customers in similar situations receive consistent treatment.

---
section: Promotion Policy — Retain & Recommend AI > 1. Purpose and Principles > 1.2 Principles

text:
## 2. Promotion Types Covered

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Percentage discount | Reduction on price of selected products or an order |
| Volume or tier incentive | Better price for purchase volume |
| Free shipping or service benefit | Non-price commercial benefit |
| Credit or rebate | Value returned after purchase |
| Bundle offer | Combination of products at a package price |
| Early-access or priority-availability benefit | Non-price benefit; no margin cost |

**`Data Gap`** — Which of these types the business actually offers is not specified.

**`Proposed Assumption`** — Non-price benefits (early access, priority availability, service attention) are lower risk to profitability and should be considered before price-based promotions.

### 3.1 Eligibility Criteria (All Must Be True)

**`Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval`** — Reactivation offers are treated as a separate decision. They require approval regardless of value tier, because the customer is outside the standard prediction population and because outcomes are hard to separate from natural return behavior.

### 4.4 Value Tier Considerations
- V1 customers: higher potential justification, but also higher exposure if margin is eroded. Require approval when the customer is on the Focus List.
- V3 customers: Default to non-price, low-cost actions. A promotion needs a documented reason.
- **Guardrail PG-3:** Value tier is derived from historical net revenue. It does not equal profit. If customer margin is unknown, say so.

- Record the rule path for each recommendation so similar cases can be checked for consistency.

## 5. Product Availability and Cancellation Considerations

### 5.1 Availability Rules
- **PG-4:** Never recommend a promotion on a product marked unavailable, discontinued, or restricted.
- **PG-5:** If stock status is unknown, mark "availability unconfirmed" and require approval; do not assume availability.
- **PG-6:** Avoid promoting products with constrained stock that would be oversold, because stock-outs lead to cancellations.
section: Promotion Policy — Retain & Recommend AI > 5. Product Availability and Cancellation Considerations > 5.1 Availability Rules

### 5.2 Cancellation-Aware Rules
`Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval`
- **PG-7:** Do not offer promotions on products with high estimated cancellation risk for that customer or segment, unless a human confirms the cause has been addressed. **`Data Gap`** — what counts as "high" cancellation risk is not defined; use model-supplied values and the thresholds approved by the business.
- **PG-8:** A promotion must not make it cheaper to place and then cancel an order. Check whether the offer conditions apply only to fulfilled (non-cancelled) orders.
- **PG-9:** Promotion effectiveness must be measured on **net** (post-cancellation) results, not gross orders.

## 7. Discount Limits, Budgets, Margins, and Profitability Safeguards

### 7.1 Limits and Budgets
**`Data Gap`** — Actual limits, budgets, and margin requirements are not provided. The framework below is structural only.

| Control | Definition | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Discount cap by tier | Maximum percentage for each promotion category | `D_MAX_[tier]` — not set |
| Minimum margin | Lowest acceptable margin after discount | `M_MIN` — not set |
| Period budget | Total promotion spend allowed | `B_PERIOD` — not set |
| Customer budget | Spend allowed per customer per period | `B_CUSTOMER` — not set |
| Cooldown | Days between promotions per customer | `N_COOLDOWN` — not set |
section: Promotion Policy — Retain & Recommend AI > 7. Discount Limits, Budgets, Margins, and Profitability Safeguards > 7.1 Limits and Budgets

text:
### 7.2 Margin Safeguard Formula (Structural)
```
Post-Promotion Margin Rate = (Net Price after Discount − Unit Cost) / Net Price after Discount
```
- `Net Price after Discount` — currency per unit, after the discount.
- `Unit Cost` — currency per unit of product cost. **`Data Gap`** — product cost data is not confirmed.
- **Unit:** ratio (0 to 1) or percentage. Denominator: net price after discount.
- **Rule:** If `Post-Promotion Margin Rate < M_MIN`, the recommendation is **Not Recommended**.
- **Limitation:** The formula ignores shipping, handling, payment, and returns costs unless they are included in unit cost.
section: Promotion Policy — Retain & Recommend AI > 7. Discount Limits, Budgets, Margins, and Profitability Safeguards > 7.2 Margin Safeguard Formula (Structural)

text:
### 7.3 Profitability Assessment Cautions
- Revenue, profit, customer value, and model scores are different things (see `business_rules_kpis.md`, Section 14).
- **PG-10:** The Agent must not claim that a promotion is profitable unless cost and margin data are supplied and the calculation is shown.
- **PG-11:** Historical net revenue of a customer does not justify a discount by itself.
- **PG-12:** Expected gains from a retained customer are `Pending Validation` until measured in a controlled evaluation.

**`Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval`** — Each approved promotion must be recorded against its budget; the Agent must check whether remaining budget information is available. If not available, mark `Data Gap` and require approval.

## 10. Approval Workflow and Auditability

### 10.1 Workflow
1. **Agent drafts** a promotion recommendation with the required fields (10.2).
2. **Eligibility check** against Sections 3 to 7.
3. **Decision matrix** outcome assigned (Section 8).
4. **Routing:** Not Recommended → record and suggest alternatives; Eligible for Review → reviewer; Requires Approval → approver at `APPROVER_ROLE_[n]` (`Data Gap`).
5. **Human decision** recorded: approved, modified, rejected, with reason.
6. **Execution** occurs outside the Agent, by authorized staff.
7. **Post-hoc review** compares outcomes with expectations, using net results and, where possible, a holdout group.

### 1.3 Ground Rules
- **Rule R-1:** This document defines *how* to compute and interpret things. It contains **no** actual customer data, model results, or performance figures. **`Verified Fact`** — none were supplied.

## 3. Core Business Concepts

### 3.1 Customer
- Unit of analysis for lapse prediction and retention.
- **Active customer:** at least one valid purchase in W_obs ending at T.
- **Already Lapsed customer:** no valid purchase in the most recent 90 days as of T. `Proposed Assumption`.
- **Limited History:** exactly one valid purchase in W_obs.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Core Business Concepts > 3.1 Customer

text:
### 3.2 Transaction
A transaction is an invoice with a timestamp, a customer, and one or more line items. A purchase transaction increases sales; a cancellation or return transaction reduces net sales.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Core Business Concepts > 3.2 Transaction

text:
### 3.3 Product
An item with an identifier and (ideally) a description, category, price, cost, and stock status. **`Data Gap`** — product category hierarchy, cost, and stock fields are unconfirmed.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Core Business Concepts > 3.3 Product

text:
### 3.4 Purchase
A valid completed sale after exclusion of cancellations, returns, test records, and other non-sales (Section 5).
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Core Business Concepts > 3.4 Purchase

text:
### 3.5 Return vs. Cancellation
| Concept | Timing | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Cancellation | Order is voided, often before or around fulfillment | Reduces net revenue; may lower fulfilment |
| Return | Goods come back after delivery | Reduces net revenue; may incur handling costs |

**`Data Gap`** — If the source does not distinguish them, treat both as "Cancellation/Return Events" and label results accordingly. The Agent must not state a cause for either.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 3. Core Business Concepts > 3.5 Return vs. Cancellation

text:
### 3.6 Cancellation Risk
The estimated likelihood that an order line for a customer-product pair is later cancelled or returned. It is used to down-rank recommendations (Section 10). It is a model output, not a fact about customer intent.

### 5.1 Preprocessing Rules
1. Build a cleaned transaction table with a `valid_purchase` flag and an `is_cancellation` flag.

## 6. Calculation Conventions

- **Time:** Days are calendar days. A "period" is the stated window ending at T unless stated.
- **Notation:** `T` prediction timestamp; `W_obs` observation window length; `H` prediction horizon; `C` set of customers in scope.
- **Currency:** All monetary values are in the source currency unless converted. `Data Gap` — currency is unconfirmed.
- **Denominators:** Every KPI definition names its denominator. If a denominator is zero, the KPI is **undefined**, not zero.
- **Small groups:** Report group size alongside any rate.
- **Missing data:** Report "not available" rather than imputing.

---
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 6. Calculation Conventions

## 7. Data Scope for Customer Population

- **Prediction population (primary):** Active customers at T (≥ 1 valid purchase in W_obs). `Proposed Assumption`.
- **Out of scope for lapse prediction:** Already Lapsed customers (handled by reactivation guidance) and customers without customer ID.
- **Limitation:** Customers acquired shortly before T have little history; flag with the Limited History Flag.

---
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 7. Data Scope for Customer Population

## 8. Customer Lapse Prediction Definitions

### 8.1 Time Structure
```
        |<---------- W_obs ---------->|T|<---------- H ---------->|
   features computed here (≤ T)          label observed here (> T)
```

| Element | Definition | Proposed value | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prediction timestamp (T) | Date when features are frozen and a prediction is made | Set per run | `Verified Fact` that it must be explicit |
| Observation window (W_obs) | Days before T used for features | 180 days | `Proposed Assumption`, `Pending Validation` |
| Prediction horizon (H) | Days after T over which lapse is observed | 90 days | `Proposed Assumption`, `Pending Validation` |
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 8. Customer Lapse Prediction Definitions > 8.1 Time Structure

text:
### 8.2 Label Definition
```
lapse_label(c, T) = 1  if customer c is Active at T and has 0 valid purchases in (T, T + H]
lapse_label(c, T) = 0  if customer c is Active at T and has ≥ 1 valid purchase in (T, T + H]
```
- Only Active customers at T are labeled.
- A customer's final label is observable only after T + H has passed. Cohorts where T + H is in the future are **censored** and must not be used for training or evaluation.
- Cancelled purchases do not count as valid purchases.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 8. Customer Lapse Prediction Definitions > 8.2 Label Definition

text:
### 8.3 Model Output
`p_lapse(c, T)` is the estimated probability that `lapse_label(c, T) = 1`.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 8. Customer Lapse Prediction Definitions > 8.3 Model Output

text:
### 8.4 Calibration Requirement
**`Pending Validation`** — Reading risk tiers (Section 9) as real probabilities assumes `p_lapse` is calibrated, meaning that among customers with p_lapse near 0.7, about 70% actually lapse. In the supplied file the probabilities range from about 0.00000002 to 0.9996, which can indicate an over-confident model. If calibration is not confirmed, use the tiers and `p_lapse` as a ranking aid and use the percentile rank (Section 9.1) for urgency, and state this.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 8. Customer Lapse Prediction Definitions > 8.4 Calibration Requirement

text:
### 8.5 Choice of H and W_obs
**`Proposed Assumption`** — The values 90 and 180 days are starting points. They should be validated against customers' typical inter-purchase intervals: if many customers normally buy less often than every 90 days, H is too short and produces false lapse signals. **`Data Gap`** — the real distribution of inter-purchase intervals is unknown.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 8. Customer Lapse Prediction Definitions > 8.5 Choice of H and W_obs

text:
### 8.6 Already Lapsed Customers
A customer with no valid purchase in the most recent 90 days as of T. `Proposed Assumption`. Not scored by the lapse model; handled under reactivation.

| Medium | 0.30 ≤ p_lapse < 0.50 | 548 | 10.5% |
| High | p_lapse ≥ 0.50 | 4,019 | 77.0% |

Applied to the supplied file, that scheme would place 2,055 customers (39.3%) in a Critical tier, which exceeds realistic review capacity. The draft was retired. text:
Urgency within the High tier is handled by the Focus List and by the percentile rank below.
**Urgency Percentile** (descriptive, no calibration needed):
```
Urgency Percentile(c) = percent rank of p_lapse(c) among all scored customers in the same snapshot
```
- Unit: percentile, 0 to 100. Higher means a higher p_lapse relative to other customers in that snapshot.
- Limitation: It is relative to one snapshot and says nothing about the absolute chance of lapse.

**Focus List** (`Proposed Assumption`):
```
Focus List = the N High-risk customers with the highest Priority Score
```
- N is set by the business (`Data Gap`). Priority Score is defined in Section 9.3.
- If value data is not available, order High-risk customers by p_lapse and state that value was not considered.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 9. Risk Segmentation > 9.1 Risk Tier Thresholds

text:
### 9.2 Value Tier Definition
```
V_norm(c) = percentile rank of monetary_W(c) among active customers, scaled to (0, 1]
```
| Tier | Rule |
|---|---|
| V1 | V_norm ≥ 0.90 |
| V2 | 0.60 ≤ V_norm < 0.90 |
| V3 | V_norm < 0.60 |

- `monetary_W(c)` = net revenue (valid purchases minus cancellations/returns) for customer c in W_obs. Unit: currency.
- **Limitation:** Historical value is not profit or future value (Section 14). Ties and small populations affect percentiles.
- **Alternative:** If margin data is available, a margin-based value measure may be used; this is a change requiring business approval.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 9. Risk Segmentation > 9.2 Value Tier Definition

### 9.3 Priority Matrix
`Proposed Assumption`, `Pending Validation`.

| Risk \ Value | V1 | V2 | V3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | P1 | P2 | P3 |
| Medium | P2 | P3 | P4 |
| Low | P3 | P4 | P4 |

**Priority Score** (ordering aid within a band):
```
Priority Score = p_lapse × V_norm
```
Unit: dimensionless, range (0, 1]. Not a probability, not a monetary amount, not an expected loss.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 9. Risk Segmentation > 9.3 Priority Matrix

`Proposed Assumption`, `Pending Validation`.

| Flag | Definition | Variables |
|---|---|---|
| Repeated Cancellation Flag (RCF) | `cancel_count_W ≥ 3` **or** (`cancel_value_rate_W ≥ 0.20` **and** `invoice_count_W ≥ 3`) | See Section 13 |
| Declining Activity Flag (DAF) | `purchases_last90 / purchases_prev90 < 0.5` **or** `netrev_last90 / netrev_prev90 < 0.5`, provided `purchases_prev90 ≥ 2` | Last 90 days vs. the preceding 90 days before T |

## 10. Recommendation Ranking Logic

### 10.1 Components
| Component | Definition | Range | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `p_buy(c, i)` | Estimated purchase likelihood of product i by customer c in the recommendation horizon | 0 to 1 | Recommender model |
| `p_cancel(c, i)` | Estimated likelihood that a purchase of i by c is cancelled or returned | 0 to 1 | Cancellation model (customer-product or product-level) |
| `Value_norm(i)` | Business value indicator of product i, normalized | 0 to 1 | Margin or revenue proxy; `Data Gap` |
| `Availability_flag(i)` | 1 if available, 0 if unavailable/restricted/unconfirmed | {0, 1} | Stock data; `Data Gap` |
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 10. Recommendation Ranking Logic > 10.1 Components

text:
### 10.2 Adjusted Recommendation Score

`Proposed Assumption`, `Pending Validation`.

```

Adjusted Recommendation Score(c, i) = p_buy(c, i) × (1 − p_cancel(c, i)) × Value_norm(i) × Availability_flag(i)

```

- **Unit:** dimensionless score in [0, 1]. Used only to rank products for a given customer.

- **Interpretation:** Higher means "relatively better candidate" given likelihood of purchase, likelihood of the sale surviving cancellation, and value.

- **Not** a probability of sale, expected revenue, or profit. The product of the terms assumes independence, which is a simplification.

- **Fallbacks:**

  - If `Value_norm` is unavailable: set to 1 for all products and state that value was not considered.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 10. Recommendation Ranking Logic > 10.2 Adjusted Recommendation Score

text:
If `Value_norm` is unavailable: set to 1 for all products and state that value was not considered.
  - If `p_cancel` is unavailable: omit the term and state the recommendation is not cancellation-aware.

  - If `Availability_flag` is unavailable: mark "availability unconfirmed" and do not present as confirmed.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 10. Recommendation Ranking Logic > 10.2 Adjusted Recommendation Score

text:
### 10.3 Ranking Rules
1. Exclude products with `Availability_flag = 0`.
2. Rank remaining products by Adjusted Recommendation Score, descending.
3. Break ties by `p_buy`, then by lower `p_cancel`.
4. Optionally exclude products the customer already buys on every order, unless replenishment is the goal. `Proposed Assumption`.
5. Keep the list short; list length is a `Data Gap`.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 10. Recommendation Ranking Logic > 10.3 Ranking Rules

text:
### 10.4 Limitations
- Recommendation scores depend on model quality (`Pending Validation`).
- Offline ranking metrics do not prove that recommendations change purchasing.
- The cancellation term corrects for expected cancellations; it does not explain them.

---
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 10. Recommendation Ranking Logic > 10.4 Limitations

### 12.1 Historical Customer Value
```
monetary_W(c) = Net Revenue of customer c in W_obs
```

Unit: currency. **`Verified Fact`** — this is a historical measure; it does not predict future spend or profit.

```
Top-k% Revenue Share = (Σ monetary_W for the top k% customers) / (Σ monetary_W for all active customers)
```
- Unit: ratio (0 to 1). Denominator: total net revenue of active customers in W_obs.
- Use to understand dependence on top customers. **`Data Gap`** — actual concentration is unknown; any claim about it requires computed data.

### 14.2 Rules for the AI Agent
- **Rule M-1:** Never express a probability or score in currency terms.
- **Rule M-2:** Never multiply a probability by revenue and present the product as "money at risk" or "expected loss". `Verified Fact` — such a figure depends on calibration, causal assumptions, and horizon matching that have not been validated here.

| Metric | Definition | How to interpret | Limitations |

|---|---|---|---|

| ROC-AUC | Probability a random lapsing customer is scored higher than a random non-lapsing one | 0.5 = no better than chance; higher is better ranking | Can look good with imbalanced classes; ignores calibration |

| PR-AUC | Area under the precision–recall curve | Compare to the lapse base rate | Sensitive to class prevalence |

| Precision | `TP / (TP + FP)` | Among flagged customers, share that truly lapsed | Depends on threshold |

| Recall | `TP / (TP + FN)` | Share of lapsing customers that were flagged | Depends on threshold |

### 15.3 Temporal Validation Rules

`Proposed Policy — Requires Business Approval`

1. **Split by time, never at random.** Train on earlier prediction timestamps and validate/test on later ones.

2. **Use multiple prediction timestamps** (rolling-origin / backtesting) to check stability across seasons. Number of folds `Data Gap`.

3. **Gap between training and testing:** Ensure the label period of training samples ends before the test T. Otherwise the future leaks into training.

4. **Censoring:** Exclude samples whose T + H lies beyond the last available data date.

5. **Customer overlap:** The same customers appear at multiple timestamps; consider customer-grouped evaluation to measure generalization to new customers, in addition to time-based splits.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 15. Model Evaluation, Temporal Validation, and Limitations > 15.3 Temporal Validation Rules

text:

6. **Preprocessing fit on training data only:** For example, percentiles, scalers, and encodings.

7. **Hyperparameter selection on validation periods only;** the final test period is used once.

### 15.4 Data Leakage Prevention

| Leakage type | Example | Prevention |

|---|---|---|

| Future data in features | Counting purchases after T | Compute features with timestamp ≤ T only |

| Label overlap | Using H-period behavior in features | Strict window separation |

| Post-event fields | Fields created after outcome (for example, account status set after lapse) | Review each field's creation time (`Data Gap`) |

| Cancellation timing | A cancellation after T that reverses a purchase before T | Use information as known at T; define rules for late cancellations |

| Global statistics | Percentiles computed on all data including future | Compute within training data/prior to T |

| Identifier leakage | IDs that encode time or customer age | Review features |

| Identifier leakage | IDs that encode time or customer age | Review features |
| Duplicate customers across splits | Same customer in train and test at close times | Group or time-gap splits |
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 15. Model Evaluation, Temporal Validation, and Limitations > 15.4 Data Leakage Prevention

text:
### 15.5 Evaluation Limitations
- **No causal claims:** Predictive accuracy does not show that interventions work.
- **Base rate sensitivity:** Metrics depend on the lapse rate, which varies by period.
- **Seasonality and shocks:** A single period may not represent future periods.
- **Calibration drift:** Probabilities may degrade over time; monitor.
- **Selection effects:** Offline evaluation on historical data cannot reveal effects of recommendations that were never shown.
- **Business-value gap:** Good metrics do not guarantee business benefit; measure outcomes with a holdout (`Pending Validation`).
- **Small groups:** High-value segments are small, so metrics for them are noisy.
- **Fairness and consistency:** Check performance across customer segments. `Proposed Assumption`.
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 15. Model Evaluation, Temporal Validation, and Limitations > 15.5 Evaluation Limitations

text:
### 15.6 Monitoring (Proposed)
`Proposed Assumption` — Track data quality, score distributions, calibration, and tier shares over time, and trigger review when they shift materially. Thresholds `Data Gap`.

---
section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 15. Model Evaluation, Temporal Validation, and Limitations > 15.6 Monitoring (Proposed)

### 16.1 Principle
Every AI-generated recommendation must be traceable to (a) the rule or guidance used, (b) the data inputs, and (c) the model output. This enables audits, debugging, and trust.

### 16.5 Traceability Rules
- **T-1:** Every customer-specific statement in an Agent output must cite its data source (model output or structured data field).
- **T-2:** Every business guidance statement must cite the Knowledge Base section.
- **T-3:** Statements without a source must be marked as assumptions or omitted.
- **T-4:** If the Knowledge Base and the data disagree (for example, thresholds differ), report the conflict and apply human review (`HR-6` / `HR-10`).

## 19. Questions This Document Can Answer

text:
### 19.1 Definitions and Terminology

- What do prediction timestamp, observation window and prediction horizon mean?

### 19.2 The Supplied Scoring File
- What columns does `customer_lapse_predictions.csv` contain and what do they mean?

text:

- Which fields are needed for each KPI?

- How are gross revenue, net revenue, AOV and purchase frequency calculated, with which denominator?

section: Business Rules and KPIs — Retain & Recommend AI > 19. Questions This Document Can Answer > 19.5 Segmentation and Ranking
